messages.raw: {"reply":"The dossier lists three panels: Larkspur, Quill, and Sedge. Each tray held the panel on a raised polyester mesh, two damp cellulose blotters under the mesh, one dry blotter above the panel edge, a humidity indicator strip, an ID tag, and a side well with 20 mL distilled water. Panels began in the damp room for 24 hours, then were transferred to the dry room at t=0. They were repositioned at t=30 and t=90 minutes, returned to the damp room at t=180, and the cycle was repeated on two further days. Photographs were taken at t=-15, t=0, t=30, t=60, t=120, and t=180, with one overhead shot and one raking-light edge shot per time point, including a 100 mm scale bar. Repeat observations were recorded six times per cycle, for three cycles per panel, giving eighteen observations per panel. One recorded observation for each panel is: Larkspur at t=60 had upper-corner lift of 2.3 mm, moisture reading 11.4 percent, and curl radius 820 mm. Quill at t=60 had an edge gap increase from 0.4 mm to 1.1 mm, bow of 3.0 mm over a 300 mm straightedge, and room RH 32 percent. Sedge at t=120 showed surface ripple spacing of 60 mm, ripple amplitude 0.8 mm, and mass loss of 1.2 g from the t=0 mass."}
